blurb: Wolfdog breed developed from crosses of Carpathian wolves and German Shepherds
description: The Czechoslovakian Wolfdog is a wolfdog breed from Czechoslovakia, bred from Carpathian wolves and German Shepherds, with a thick silver-grey coat.
answer: The Czechoslovakian Wolfdog is a breed of wolfdog that began as a 1955 military experiment in Czechoslovakia crossing a Carpathian grey wolf with a German Shepherd. It is a large dog, with a breed standard minimum of 65 cm for males and 60 cm for females. Sources give little detail about its temperament.

body: In 1955 Colonel Karel Hartl, working with cynologist Heiri Machat, began an experiment in military kennels in Czechoslovakia to cross a Carpathian grey wolf with a German Shepherd. The first hybrids, from a female wolf named Brita and a sable German Shepherd named Cézar, were born on 26 May 1958. Known as the Czech Wolfdog until 1982, it became a recognized national breed that year and was accepted by the FCI in 1999 in its Sheepdogs and Cattledogs group. The American Kennel Club published a breed standard in 2024.

The standard sets minimum heights at the withers of 65 cm for males and 60 cm for females, with minimum weights of 26 kg and 20 kg. The coat is straight and close-fitting, very thick in winter and thinner in summer. Color ranges from silver-grey to yellow-grey, or dark grey, always with a light mask and light hair on the chest and under the neck.

The available sources say little about temperament. Some of these dogs have been used in search-and-rescue work in the United Kingdom. Anyone interested in the breed is generally advised to consult the breed standard and breed clubs for a description of its character.

Sources give little detail on care. As a large working-type dog descended from German Shepherds and wolves, it is generally expected to need regular exercise, and its coat changes noticeably between the thick winter coat and the thinner summer coat.

The available sources do not describe specific health conditions in the breed. Breed clubs generally recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups. A 2015 DNA study found limited genetic diversity in its maternal and paternal lines.

faq.q: Is the Czechoslovakian Wolfdog part wolf?
faq.a: Yes. The breed was created by crossing Carpathian grey wolves with German Shepherds, followed by backcrossing to German Shepherds.

faq.q: Is the Czechoslovakian Wolfdog recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI definitively accepted it in 1999 as breed number 332 in Group 1, Sheepdogs and Cattledogs.

faq.q: How big is a Czechoslovakian Wolfdog?
faq.a: The standard calls for a minimum height of 65 cm and weight of 26 kg for males, and 60 cm and 20 kg for females.
